attacker.description: An attacker on the internet guesses a weak SSH password on a shop's web server, looks around, finds a deploy key, uses it to pull the build server's configuration, and uploads it out over HTTPS, while Wazuh watches web, build and db. The engine ran the path's 11 steps in turn inside the sealed range range-one, through docker exec as the step's account. The steps ran 10 published tests.

steps.title: SSH Credential Stuffing From Linux
steps.plain: From the attacker's machine, tries each user name and password of a published list on web's SSH server, and gets in as webadmin.
steps.command: cp "/opt/atomics/T1110.004/src/credstuffuserpass.txt" /tmp/; for unamepass in $(cat /tmp/credstuffuserpass.txt);do sshpass -p `echo $unamepass | cut -d":" -f2` ssh -o 'StrictHostKeyChecking=no' `echo $unamepass | cut -d":" -f1`@web;done

notes: Hand-off: steps s02 to s10 run as webadmin on web through docker exec, not inside the SSH session of s01.
The engine's own executor ran each step, reading the test as Invoke-AtomicRedTeam 8af478bb9e4637df568ac1e596553b025b16cd1b does; the atomic-parity job of the range one workflow checks that.
Each test runs through docker exec as the step's account: its parent is the container runtime, not a login shell, and no step runs inside the session of an earlier one.
A step's start and end are the Docker daemon's times of its exec_start and exec_die events, when they are in order; otherwise the engine's, and the step's time_source says so.
blocked cannot occur: the range configures no active response.
An effect check that exits nonzero counts as no effect, also when it could not find the file it reads; only a check that could not be run at all makes a step inconclusive.

Events are tied to a step by snoopy's tag of its session, the accounts only the path uses, the address or container name of the host it ran on and the paths it was given, inside its time span, from its start to 5 s after its end; an event that only falls inside that time span is coincident and never counts.
This top-level Wazuh detail uses no network sensor, so scans and exfiltrations are seen here only through what they leave in the logs and files the agents watch.
Snoopy misses the first program of each docker exec, the published sh -c itself, which is the step's command.
The defense is the stock Wazuh rules with the lab's agent configuration (its diff is in the manifest). One run is one sample: variation between runs is not yet shown.

The steps' times are the Docker daemon's and the alerts' the manager container's: 19 program starts snoopy logged in the steps' sessions, at their containers' time, all fall inside their step's daemon times.
An alert's time is the time of the event it was raised on, and raised is the manager's time of it: the race counts to raised.

889 archived events fell only inside a step's time span, from its start to 5 s after its end, on a host it ran on or reached: coincident in time, not counted as the step's and not in the recording; events.ecs.ndjson holds them with the step and tied_by window.

3 steps had more than 300 events. The recording keeps the first 300 of each, shared in equal parts among the sensors that recorded them, and every event a rule matched; events.ecs.ndjson and events.network.ecs.ndjson.gz hold them all.

5 defenses judged this one run, each counting only the events of its own sensors and the alerts of its own detectors: Wazuh with its stock rules (wazuh-stock); Public Sigma rules on host logs (sigma-public); Packets on web, judged by Suricata with the ET Open rules (packets-et-open); AI tool detection packs on host logs and packets (ai-tool-packs); Ordered credential activity on host logs (ordered-credential). The top level of the recording is the first, wazuh-stock.
